answer: Each PoA task commits to a domain-separated hash of its task ID and a future drand quicknet threshold-BLS pulse. Only after the pulse is finalized does the network derive the challenge and open a bounded commit-reveal window. This blocks advance computation and offline answer hoarding; per-task resource costs and verified completion—not addresses alone—make spawning sybils unprofitable. The prism, tundra, and nadir labels separate challenge domains; the beacon supplies unpredictability, not identity.
